---
name: a3-course-grounded-drafting
description: Capture the author's judgements and draft one Assignment 3 section at a time from the template, ledger, course notes, reuse proposals and public evidence, within stated word caps and with every claim tagged. Includes the public-evidence research protocol for A3, C1 and C2.
---
<purpose>
Produce a section draft that is specific, evidence-disciplined, within its cap, consistent with the ledger and written from the author's own judgements.
</purpose>

<trigger>
Per section at its gate, in dependency order (A, B, C, D), after G2 and G3. Research for A3, C1 and C2 may run earlier.
</trigger>

<inputs>
- template section (fields, caps, descriptor atoms, layout recommendation)
- ledger slice for the section's dependencies
- course notes (Modules 1, 2, 3) cited as "course notes"
- reuse proposals for the section
- the author's answers to judgement-capture questions
- public sources found through web search (research protocol)
</inputs>

<procedure>
1. Read the section's template entry and the ledger slice. List dependencies and check they are approved. If not, stop.
2. Judgement capture: return to the agent a short list of questions with options and the evidence behind each (ratings, classifications, ranks, positions, role, framework). Draft nothing that depends on an unanswered judgement.
3. Draft in the layout recommended in the template (table or labelled paragraph, worksheet field labels verbatim). Put surplus detail in an <appendix> block below the response; the main text must stand alone.
4. Use course definitions as the worksheet states them (Quick Win, Strategic Bet, Moonshot; automatable, augmentable, irreducibly human; Lead, Fast follow, Wait). Cite course concepts as course notes. Verify any statistic from notes before presenting it as external fact; otherwise mark it "per course notes".
5. Tag every factual claim: [D:ref] documented in prior work; [C:ref] course notes; [E:ID] public evidence; [A:ID] assumption; [F:ID] ledger figure; [J] author judgement. Use [R:Dimension=Rating] and [L:OppID=Classification] when a rating or classification is stated.
6. Rephrase prior content; no verbatim reuse; professional tone matched to the assignment.
7. Public-evidence protocol (A3, C1, C2): search only public, current, identifiable sources; record for each: title, organisation, date, URL, access date, section used; assign the next E-ID; if no usable source exists write "Not evidenced" or "Not applicable". Never infer a competitor signal. Treat press releases as one weak source type; prefer multiple signal types (patents, hiring, product, filings, structured CI).
8. Count words against the stated cap (tags and appendix excluded). Reduce before returning.
9. Return: draft, claim-tag sheet, word count, proposed ledger entries (including E-IDs, assumptions, figures), open questions.
</procedure>

<outputs>
Draft content in the recommended layout; claim-tag sheet; word count; proposed ledger entries; open questions.
</outputs>

<exclusions>
Decides no rating, classification, priority, position, role or framework. No headcount-reduction framing. No unsourced competitor or benchmark claim. No ROI/vendor/governance-model content. No ledger writes. No declaration or disclosure text for signature.
</exclusions>

<acceptance_checks>
- Within the stated cap; every field filled; zero placeholders.
- Every factual claim tagged; every public claim has an E-ID with title, organisation, date and URL, or reads "Not evidenced".
- Ratings and classifications match the ledger and the author's recorded judgement.
- Worksheet definitions used as stated; field labels verbatim.
- No verbatim passages from prior work or notes.
</acceptance_checks>

<escalation>
Ask the author when evidence is missing for a mandatory field, when sources conflict, when a claim would exceed the declared scope, or when a figure cannot be traced.
</escalation>
